landmarks.name: Empire State Building
landmarks.fact: Opened in 1931 and held the title of world's tallest building for nearly 40 years.

landmarks.name: Chrysler Building
landmarks.fact: An Art Deco tower that was briefly the tallest building in the world in 1930.

landmarks.name: Times Square
landmarks.fact: Named after The New York Times, which moved its headquarters here in 1904.

landmarks.name: Grand Central Terminal
landmarks.fact: Opened in 1913. The main concourse ceiling is painted with the constellations.

landmarks.name: New York Public Library (Main Branch)
landmarks.fact: Opened in 1911. Its marble lions are named Patience and Fortitude.

landmarks.name: Bryant Park
landmarks.fact: A park built directly on top of the library's underground book stacks.

landmarks.name: Rockefeller Center
landmarks.fact: Its Christmas tree tradition dates back to the 1930s.

landmarks.name: St. Patrick's Cathedral
landmarks.fact: A Gothic Revival cathedral dedicated in 1879.

landmarks.name: Museum of Modern Art
landmarks.fact: Founded in 1929; home to Van Gogh's The Starry Night.

landmarks.name: Carnegie Hall
landmarks.fact: Opened in 1891, with Tchaikovsky conducting on opening night.

landmarks.name: Columbus Circle
landmarks.fact: The official point from which distances from New York City are measured.

landmarks.name: United Nations Headquarters
landmarks.fact: The Secretariat building opened in 1952 on the East River.

landmarks.name: The Vessel, Hudson Yards
landmarks.fact: A honeycomb of 154 connected flights of stairs, opened in 2019.

landmarks.name: Madison Square Garden
landmarks.fact: The arena sits directly on top of Penn Station.

landmarks.name: Lincoln Center
landmarks.fact: Built in the 1950s and 60s on land cleared from the San Juan Hill neighborhood.

landmarks.name: American Museum of Natural History
landmarks.fact: Founded in 1869; famous for its dinosaur halls.

landmarks.name: Strawberry Fields
landmarks.fact: A memorial to John Lennon with a mosaic reading Imagine.

landmarks.name: Bethesda Terrace
landmarks.fact: Its Angel of the Waters was made by Emma Stebbins, the first woman to receive a public art commission in New York City.

landmarks.name: Belvedere Castle
landmarks.fact: Built in 1869 as a lookout; it now hosts a weather station.

landmarks.name: Central Park Zoo
landmarks.fact: A small zoo in the southeast corner of the park.

landmarks.name: The Metropolitan Museum of Art
landmarks.fact: Founded in 1870; the largest art museum in the United States.

landmarks.name: Guggenheim Museum
landmarks.fact: Designed by Frank Lloyd Wright as a spiral ramp; opened in 1959.

landmarks.name: Columbia University
landmarks.fact: Founded in 1754 as King's College.

landmarks.name: Cathedral of St. John the Divine
landmarks.fact: Construction began in 1892 and the cathedral is still unfinished.

landmarks.name: Grant's Tomb
landmarks.fact: The resting place of President Ulysses S. Grant, and the largest mausoleum in North America.

landmarks.name: Apollo Theater
landmarks.fact: Its Amateur Night has been launching careers since 1934.

landmarks.name: Morris-Jumel Mansion
landmarks.fact: Manhattan's oldest surviving house, built in 1765. Washington used it as his headquarters in 1776.

landmarks.name: Little Red Lighthouse
landmarks.fact: A small lighthouse under the George Washington Bridge, made famous by a 1942 children's book.

landmarks.name: The Met Cloisters
landmarks.fact: The Met's museum of medieval art, opened in 1938.

landmarks.name: Inwood Hill Park
landmarks.fact: Home to the last natural forest in Manhattan.

landmarks.name: The High Line
landmarks.fact: An old elevated freight railway turned into a park; its first section opened in 2009.

landmarks.name: Chelsea Market
landmarks.fact: A former Nabisco factory, where the Oreo cookie was created in 1912.

landmarks.name: Little Island
landmarks.fact: A park on concrete 'tulips' in the Hudson River, opened in 2021.

landmarks.name: Flatiron Building
landmarks.fact: A triangular skyscraper completed in 1902.

landmarks.name: Union Square
landmarks.fact: Home to the city's best-known Greenmarket.

landmarks.name: Washington Square Arch
landmarks.fact: Built to mark the centennial of George Washington's inauguration; the marble arch was finished in 1892.

landmarks.name: Stonewall Inn
landmarks.fact: Site of the 1969 uprising; the first U.S. national monument to LGBTQ history.

landmarks.name: Katz's Delicatessen
landmarks.fact: A deli serving pastrami on the Lower East Side since 1888.

landmarks.name: Tenement Museum
landmarks.fact: Tells the stories of immigrant families who lived at 97 Orchard Street.

landmarks.name: Doyers Street
landmarks.fact: Its sharp bend was nicknamed the Bloody Angle during the tong wars of the early 1900s.

landmarks.name: African Burial Ground
landmarks.fact: An 18th-century burial ground for free and enslaved Africans, rediscovered in 1991.

landmarks.name: City Hall
landmarks.fact: Completed in 1812, it still houses the mayor's office.

landmarks.name: Brooklyn Bridge entrance
landmarks.fact: The bridge opened in 1883 and was the longest suspension bridge in the world at the time.

landmarks.name: 9/11 Memorial & the Oculus
landmarks.fact: The memorial's two pools sit in the footprints of the Twin Towers.

landmarks.name: New York Stock Exchange
landmarks.fact: Wall Street is named for a wall the Dutch built here in the 1600s.

landmarks.name: Charging Bull
landmarks.fact: Artist Arturo Di Modica installed it without permission in 1989.

landmarks.name: Fraunces Tavern
landmarks.fact: Where George Washington bid farewell to his officers in 1783.

landmarks.name: Castle Clinton
landmarks.fact: A fort that became America's first immigration station, decades before Ellis Island.

Find the burial ground rediscovered by construction workers in 1991.
